title: Longboard surfboard – User manual
data:
This manual explains how to use your longboard surfboard. Stable longboard for trim, glide, and classic nose-riding lines.

Getting started
1. On PU fiberglass and EPS epoxy models, wax the deck with basecoat, then a temperature-matched top coat. On the soft-top foam model, skip the wax: the foam deck provides grip.
2. Carry the board under your arm with the fins facing away from your body.
3. Paddle from the middle of the board and take a few strokes before the wave lifts the tail.
4. Pop up smoothly and step forward gradually to trim along the face.

Safety and good practice
Always surf with a leash, stay aware of other surfers and keep a safe distance from rocks and the shore break. Check the board for dings and the fins for tightness before every session.

Keep this manual for future reference. If you are unsure about any step, ask your surf shop before using the product.
author: Seastone Works Product Documentation

title: Longboard surfboard – Maintenance guide
data:
Regular care keeps your longboard surfboard performing well and extends its life. Follow these steps after every session or as indicated.

Care steps
1. Rinse with fresh water after every session, including the fin box.
2. Store out of direct sun and never leave the board in a closed car.
3. Check the rails, nose and tail for dings before each session.
4. On waxed models, strip and re-wax the deck every few weeks, or when the wax turns gritty.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.

data:

title: Repair guide for EPS epoxy surfboards
data:
EPS epoxy boards have a closed-cell foam core wrapped in epoxy resin, which makes them light and durable but sensitive to the wrong repair materials. Polyester resin can dissolve EPS foam, so use only epoxy-compatible or UV-cure repair products. This guide applies to every EPS epoxy board in the catalog.

Steps
1. Dry the board fully. Wet foam will trap water and stain, so leave the damaged area to dry for at least 24 hours in a warm, shaded place.
2. Sand the damaged area back to sound material with 80-grit paper, extending 2 cm beyond the ding. Wipe clean with a dry cloth.
3. Fill small dings with epoxy-compatible resin or UV-cure resin. For larger holes, mix the epoxy repair kit and apply it with a spreader.
4. For cracks and delaminations, cut fiberglass cloth slightly larger than the repair and saturate it with epoxy.
5. Cure fully (epoxy: 12 to 24 hours; UV resin: a few minutes in direct sun). Sand with 120-grit, then 220-grit paper until the repair is flush with the surface.

Never use polyester resin or solvent-based fillers on EPS foam. If the core is exposed over a large area or the board is waterlogged, take it to a qualified repairer.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.
author: Seastone Works Product Documentation

title: Repair guide for PU fiberglass surfboards
data:
PU fiberglass boards have a polyurethane foam core and a polyester resin shell. They are traditional, responsive and easy to repair at home with fiberglass cloth and compatible resin. This guide applies to every PU fiberglass board in the catalog.

Steps
1. Dry the damaged area. Water absorbed by PU foam turns it yellow and weakens the board, so let it dry for at least 24 hours before repairing.
2. Sand around the ding with 80-grit paper to remove loose glass and expose clean fiberglass.
3. Cut fiberglass cloth slightly larger than the damaged area. Mix polyester resin with catalyst and saturate the cloth on the board.
4. Squeegee out the excess resin and let it cure in a ventilated, shaded place. UV-cure resin is a quicker option for small dings.
5. Sand the cured repair with 120-grit then 220-grit paper to blend it into the board. Apply wax or a traction pad when finished.

Polyester resin is flammable and gives off fumes: work outdoors or in a well-ventilated area and wear gloves and eye protection. Large cracks, stringer damage and broken tails should be assessed by a qualified repairer.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.

title: Care guide for soft-top foam surfboards
data:
Soft-top boards have a foam deck over a lightweight core, so they are forgiving and durable but sensitive to heat and solvents. This guide applies to every soft-top foam board in the catalog, including the soft-top beginner and foamie boards.

Steps
1. Rinse with fresh water after every session and let the board dry in the shade.
2. Clean the deck with mild soap and a soft brush. Do not use solvents, abrasive pads or wax removers.
3. Never leave a soft-top board in a closed car or in direct summer sun: heat can bubble the deck or warp the bottom.
4. Do not apply surf wax to the deck; the foam provides its own grip.
5. Store the board flat or on a padded rack. Do not stack heavy items on top.

Small compressions and surface scratches are normal and do not affect performance. If the deck delaminates or the bottom skin tears, stop using the board and contact the shop.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.

title: Care guide for carbon sandwich surfboards
data:
Carbon sandwich boards use a carbon-fibre layer over a lightweight core to create a stiff, high-performance board. They resist deformation but can crack under point impacts. This guide applies to every carbon sandwich board in the catalog.

Steps
1. Rinse with fresh water after each session and wipe the board dry.
2. Inspect rails, nose and tail after each session. Carbon cracks look like hairline lines, often with a lighter patch beneath.
3. Keep the board shaded and never leave it in a closed vehicle.
4. Use a padded board bag and avoid hard contact with rocks, racks and other boards.
5. Have any crack assessed by a qualified repairer. Do not apply regular resin to carbon yourself.

Carbon dust is an irritant: wear a mask and gloves if you sand any part of the board.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.

title: Care guide for fiberglass fins
data:
Fiberglass fins are durable, flexible and affordable. They flex under load, which gives a forgiving feel but means the tips can chip or delaminate with hard impacts. This guide applies to every fiberglass fin in the catalog.

Steps
1. Remove the fins from the board after each session and rinse with fresh water.
2. Dry the fins and the fin boxes. Sand left in a box will stop the fins from seating properly.
3. Inspect the leading edge, tip and base. Inspect the trailing edge for cracks and the base for loose tabs.
4. Store the fins in a case or the board bag, not loose.
5. Replace the screws and plates if they show corrosion.

Fins are sharp. Handle them with care and keep them away from skin and board surfaces.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.

title: Installation guide for nylon composite fin boxes
data:
Nylon composite fin boxes are the standard-tier option. They bond well to PU and epoxy boards and flex slightly, which helps absorb shocks. This guide applies to every nylon composite fin box in the catalog. Installation requires basic repair skills; consider asking a surf shop repairer to do it.

Steps
1. Remove the old fin box by routing around it, taking care not to damage the stringer.
2. Clean the pocket and sand the surface to remove loose fibres. Dry-fit the new box with a fin to check alignment.
3. Mix resin that is compatible with the board's construction (epoxy resin for EPS epoxy boards, polyester or epoxy for PU boards).
4. Press the box into the pocket and wipe away the excess resin. Hold it in place with tape until it sets.
5. Allow the resin to cure completely before fitting fins or surfing. Sand the surrounding area flush.

A box that is not aligned with the other boxes will cause the board to track badly. Dry-fit with fins before applying resin.

If something does not seat or align properly, stop and check the steps again rather than forcing it. When in doubt, have a qualified surf shop technician carry out the installation.

title: Care guide for neoprene wetsuits and accessories
data:
Neoprene is a closed-cell rubber foam that keeps you warm by trapping a thin layer of water against your skin. It is sensitive to heat, sunlight and chemicals. This guide applies to every neoprene product in the catalog: wetsuits, jackets, vests, tops, pants, boots, gloves and hoods.

Steps
1. Rinse the inside and outside with fresh, cool water after every session.
2. Hang the suit on a wide-shoulder hanger or drying rack, inside out first, then flip it to dry the outside. Keep it out of direct sun.
3. Never use a washing machine, dryer, hot water, bleach or dry-cleaning solvent. Wash occasionally by hand with a neoprene-safe shampoo.
4. Lubricate zips and seals with a neoprene-safe lubricant, and repair small tears early with flexible wetsuit glue.
5. Store the suit hung or loosely folded in a cool, dry place. Avoid creasing, and do not hang by the shoulders for long periods.

Use only products labelled neoprene-safe: the catalog's wetsuit shampoo, repair glue and zipper lubricant are suitable. Cleaners and glues not made for neoprene can damage it.

Stop using the product and replace or repair it if you notice cracks, tears or other structural damage.

title: Choosing fins and fin boxes: setup and compatibility guide
data:
Your board's fin boxes decide which fins you can use. This guide explains how to match fin sets, fin boxes and hardware to your surfboard. It applies to all surfboards, fin sets, fin boxes and fin hardware in the catalog.

Steps
1. Look at the fin boxes on your board: single-box (center only), dual-tab (FinFoundry-style or HorizonTide-style) or a 2+1 layout.
2. Choose a fin set that matches the box type. Thruster, quad and twin sets fit dual-tab boxes. The single longboard fin fits a single center box.
3. Choose a setup for the waves: thruster for all-round control, quad for speed in small waves, twin for flow, single for trim.
4. Replace worn screws and plates with the surfboard fin screws and plates set, and replace damaged boxes with a compatible replacement fin box.
5. Test the fins in the water and adjust their position in the box if your board feels too stiff or too loose.

Keep this manual for future reference. If you are unsure about any step, ask your surf shop before using the product.

title: Transporting and storing your surfboard
data:
Most surfboard damage happens out of the water. This guide explains how to carry, drive with, fly with and store your surfboard safely. It applies to all surfboards and the transport and storage products in the catalog.

Steps
1. Carry the board with the fins facing your body and the deck against your hip. Use a day bag for short trips.
2. On a car, place the board fin-side up on padded roof rack bars (or a soft roof rack). Use two straps over each board, tight but not crushing, and twist the straps to reduce hum.
3. For flights, remove the fins, wrap the rails and tail, and use the airline protection kit in a padded travel bag.
4. At home, store the board indoors on a wall mount or padded rack, away from sun and heat.
5. Never leave boards in a closed car and check straps at every stop.

Keep this manual for future reference. If you are unsure about any step, ask your surf shop before using the product.

title: Cold-water use guide for 5/4/3 mm wetsuits
data:
The 5/4/3 mm wetsuits are built for cold water, usually below 10°C. This guide covers the Elite full-length wetsuit (SRF-WS-001-V03) and the hooded wetsuit (SRF-WS-007-V01).

Steps
1. Fit matters more than thickness: the suit should be snug at the neck, wrists and ankles, with no large gaps at the back or chest.
2. Wet the suit and your skin with warm water to ease dressing. Take your time getting arms and shoulders in.
3. Add boots, gloves and a hood when water is below 10°C. Cover as much skin as possible.
4. Limit your session length and exit the water if you start to shiver. Have a warm drink and a changing robe ready.
5. After surfing, rinse, hang to dry inside out and keep the suit away from heat.

Keep this manual for future reference. If you are unsure about any step, ask your surf shop before using the product.
